clue.text: Firm support for item of office equipment

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A company buys a stand for one of its office machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is a standard piece of office kit.

clue.text: Have to put lid on glue when it's upset

parts.note: to cap a jar is to put its lid on
size is a gluey wash used to prepare walls and paper

explanation.surface: A DIY warning that the glue pot must be capped in case it gets knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a boat is to upset it, the nautical sense of being tipped over.

clue.text: Three-quarters will have completed training

definitions.meaning: in rugby the three-quarter backs move the ball wide along the line, having thrown it out
military cadets finish their course with a parade, after which they are fully trained

explanation.surface: Most recruits are expected to finish their training.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the three-quarters are the backs who run with the ball, passing it out along the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets who have graduated from training are said to have left it formally on parade.

clue.text: Duty-free

parts.note: read not as tax-free goods at an airport but as free of any obligation or duty

explanation.definitionFit: Someone excused from an obligation is released from the duty, free of it.

clue.text: Launching of report on cricket side

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a blast
the off side is one half of a cricket field, the side the batter faces

explanation.surface: A news item about a cricket team, perhaps the start of a season.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The firing of a rocket at the start of its flight is its launch.

clue.text: Audible fault in circuitry

indicators.note: audible means we go by what is heard, a word said aloud

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or fault

explanation.surface: An engineer hears a fault in some electrical wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuitry' suggests electronics, but here it means runs round a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuits of a racetrack are counted one by one in a race.

clue.text: Go away, ski run is not working

parts.note: a ski run is a slope
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A skier leaves because the piste is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip away quietly is an informal idiom for leaving.

clue.text: Ring up wicked girl

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in a down clue up tells us to read the word evil from bottom to top

parts.note: wicked means evil

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a nasty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' reads like making a phone call, but 'Ring' is the letter O and 'up' turns only the word for wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's name, the crossword's stock use of 'girl'.

clue.text: Men held by strange gift-of imagination?

indicators.note: held by means one word is placed within the other
strange suggests the letters of gift are in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a strange talent in men just imagined?
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'gift-of' joins the wordplay to the definition for the surface; the definition completes the stock phrase about imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase is 'a figment of the imagination', an invented fancy.

clue.text: Bill for publicity

parts.note: a bill here is a printed notice stuck on a wall to advertise

explanation.definitionFit: A printed bill pasted up to advertise an event is a placard.

clue.text: Being hostile or just the contrary

definitions.meaning: being hostile to something means being against it
something just the contrary is the opposite, as opposite sides of a street

explanation.surface: Someone is unfriendly, or simply perverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Resisting a plan is hostility; facing ends are contrary positions.

clue.text: Preparing a cheese grill?

definitions.meaning: hard cheese is prepared by rubbing it into shreds
a grill is a metal grid or lattice over an opening

explanation.surface: A cook gets cheese ready to put under the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' looks like the kitchen grill, but it is a lattice of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredding cheese is the kitchen sense; a lattice of bars over a drain is the other.

clue.text: Clumsy former spouse in Pinter play

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another
play means the letters of Pinter move about freely

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: A divorced partner gives an awkward performance in a Harold Pinter drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter was a British playwright, so 'play' poses as a noun, though it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unskilled is clumsy or lacking expertise.

clue.text: Harsh cut with end of knife

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word knife

explanation.surface: A cruel slash with the point of a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern or harsh punishment is called a severe one.

clue.text: Understand and win popularity

definitions.meaning: to grasp an idea is to understand it
a fashion that becomes popular is said to take off with the public

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a point and becomes well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: one for grasping meaning, one for a trend spreading.

clue.text: Black bone structure

indicators.note: structure suggests the letters of bone are built into a new form

explanation.surface: A dark skeletal frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony wood is black, and the short poetic form means black.

clue.text: Standard position for a passing-out parade?

definitions.text: Standard position for a passing-out parade?

parts.words: Standard position for a passing-out parade?
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and passing out is read as dying, so the parade is a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: Flags are lowered partway down the pole to mourn a death.

clue.text: Astounded prospector is lucky, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a lucky prospector has found ore, so ore is struck

explanation.surface: A gold-hunter strikes it rich, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'ore struck' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone astonished is filled with awe, struck dumb.

clue.text: Fish from Barcelona without name

indicators.note: from tells us the fish is made out of the letters of Barcelona, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish caught off Barcelona, unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes N out of BARCELONA, leaving BARCELOA, whose letters rearrange into the fish; 'from' is a light anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-finned tuna is a sea fish.

clue.text: Nerve twice required in traffic jam

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck, as in brass neck, also means nerve or cheek

explanation.surface: It takes nerve, again and again, to cope with gridlock.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE (British slang for courage) and NECK (cheek) are two different words for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point where traffic backs up is named after a bottle's narrow top.

clue.text: Struggling weed in bed refreshed overnight?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within another
struggling suggests the letters of weed are thrown about

explanation.surface: A weed battles away in a flowerbed, revived by the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' looks like it describes the weed's growth, but it signals the anagram; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass covered in dew at dawn has been watered in the night, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Wooden support for the shaft

definitions.meaning: a heavy timber holding up a roof is a ...
a shaft of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A timber prop for a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaft' suggests a mine, but it is a shaft of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof timber and a ray of light share this word.

clue.text: Teach me to twist the knife

indicators.note: to twist means the letters of teach me are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A threat: show me how to turn the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy blade used for cutting through vegetation is a type of knife.

clue.text: African state one under matriarchal rule

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the next piece is written below

parts.note: a matriarch is a mother, and MA is mother
a law is a rule
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An African country ruled by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked southern African country is a nation state.

clue.text: Rejection upset Daniel

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of Daniel are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Daniel is hurt at being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or turning down is a rejection.

clue.text: Veto on discredited US leader

parts.note: to nix something is to veto it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ban placed on a disgraced American president.
explanation.definitionFit: This president resigned over Watergate, so he was discredited.

clue.text: Emotional act, minor as it may be

indicators.note: as it may be suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A small gesture, however minor, can still be moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sentimental and full of feeling is called romantic.

clue.text: Seek fresh increases

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of seek are made new

explanation.surface: Go looking for new pay rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke is an old verb meaning to add to or lengthen.

clue.text: You'll need a few stiff doubles at this show

definitions.text: You'll need a few stiff doubles at this show

parts.words: You'll need a few stiff doubles at this show
parts.note: stiff doubles look like strong drinks but are rigid lifelike copies of famous people

explanation.definitionFit: Madame Tussauds displays wax likenesses of celebrities.

clue.text: Blue flower?

parts.note: flower is read as something that flows, a river, and Blue recalls a Strauss waltz

explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's waltz names this river, which flows through Vienna.

clue.text: Entertainer, possibly Sudanese

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of Sudanese could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A performer who might be from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet dancer performs to entertain.

clue.text: Shellfish extract

explanation.surface: Getting the meat out of a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea snail eaten with a pin, and the idiom for prising something out.
